codeReview.summary: The f08 commit adds 5 new source files (Dock.tsx, TrainingDrawer.tsx, StatusLine.tsx, dock.css, drawer.css), updates ml-store.ts with 3 new reactive signals (noiseLevel, exampleCountSignal, lastLossSignal) and new methods (addExample, clearAll, getLossHistory), updates the debug probe with clearAll/getLossHistory, updates App.tsx with drawer state management and layout integration, and adds 22 Playwright tests covering all 8 validation assertions. The implementation is clean, well-structured, follows SolidJS conventions, and all 22 tests pass along with the full 104-test suite.

issues.description: onTrain() uses `(iml as any).isTraining` to guard against double-training. This is a type-unsafe access — `isTraining` is not declared on the WasmIML type. It works at runtime if the property exists, but could silently fail if the WASM wrapper is refactored. Consider adding `isTraining` to the WasmIML type definition or using a store-level training guard.

drawLossPlot() does not guard against division by zero when `points.length === 1` — the `points.length - 1` divisor in the x-coordinate calculation would be 0, producing Infinity/NaN for x. However, this is already guarded by `if (history.length < 2) return;` at line 68, so the `points` array (which is sliced from history) will always have length >= 2 when this line executes. No actual bug, but the slicing logic creates a subtle coupling between the early return guard and the slice.

clearAll() directly mutates WasmIML internal properties (`lossHistory.length = 0`, `lastLoss = null`, `bestLoss = null`, `totalTrainingIterations = 0`). This bypasses any encapsulation the WasmIML class might have. A dedicated `clearAll()` or `resetTrainingState()` method on WasmIML would be cleaner, but this is pragmatic given it's within the same project.

summary: PASS — Feature f08-training-drawer-controls is well-implemented. The commit adds a complete training drawer with all 5 required buttons (Add Example, Train, Clear Ex, Clear All, Randomize), a reactive status line showing example count/loss/noise, a loss plot canvas, and a 6-icon dock system. The ML store was properly extended with 3 reactive signals and 3 new methods. The debug probe was updated with clearAll() and getLossHistory(). All 22 new Playwright tests pass and cover every claimed validation assertion (VAL-TRAIN-001 through VAL-TRAIN-006, VAL-TRAIN-008, VAL-TRAIN-009). Architecture docs were updated to match. Three minor non-blocking issues noted: type-unsafe isTraining access in TrainingDrawer, direct mutation of WasmIML internals in clearAll(), and a subtle coupling in the loss plot slicing logic. None of these affect correctness.
